title: Self-Authorship Performance Map — Q2 Manager Prep (E. Chen)
text:
Purpose
- Short playbook + evidence map to drive a focused manager conversation.
- Emphasize concrete signals, mitigation plans, and 3 specific asks (growth, role scope, org support).

Key outcomes I want from the sync
- Clear expectation alignment on 'IC → lead' scope for project staffing decisions.
- Commit to a visible 6-week growth experiment (mentorship + stretch deliverable).
- Agreement on 1 resource (headcount or contractor) to unblock knowledge-transfer work.

Top signals / evidence (quick bullets I can cite)
- Ownership: Led rollout of new onboarding checklist across 4 hiring cohorts (reduced first-week time-to-first-task from ~3.2 -> ~1.9 days) — see HR-4821 epic notes.
- Impact: Co-designed manager calibration rubric used in 12 hires this cycle; documented examples of scoring edge cases (Confluence page above).
- Cross-team: Ran 3 design sessions with Eng-Console and SRE to surface compliance gaps; produced TL;DR and follow-up actions (linked PR).
- Coaching: 1:1s with 6 new managers; two reported improved hiring interview consistency (anecdotal).

Behavioral stories (short, memorable)
- "The late-sprint rescue": stepped in to restructure the candidate matrix when offer timelines slipped; negotiated compressed interview loop.
- "The template that scaled": turned a single manager checklist into a templated playbook adopted by hiring leads.

Gaps / risk signals to surface
- Bandwidth: ~35% of time spent on reactive deskwork (vendor emails, calendar triage) vs strategic initiatives.
- Visibility: No clear owner for cross-functional onboarding docs — risk of divergence.
- Measurement: We lack consistent post-hire metrics beyond 30-day NPS; need 3-month retention/engagement signals.

Draft asks (framed as concrete requests)
- Short-term: sponsor 6-week "onboarding harmonization" experiment (2 days/wk of a contractor for doc consolidation).
- Mid-term: promotion calibration conversation in April — confirm what evidence to prioritize (scope vs leadership signals).
- Support: time-block for 1 afternoon/wk for deep work; agreement to triage low-value meetings to alternate owners.

Experiment plan (6 weeks)
- Week 1: audit current onboarding docs, collect top-5 pain points from hiring leads (Slack pulse + 5 interviews).
- Weeks 2–3: create consolidated playbook + templates; run 2 pilot hiring loops.
- Weeks 4–5: measure time-to-first-task, new-hire manager satisfaction, and candidate funnel friction.
- Week 6: present results + decision: keep/iterate/scale.

Evidence snippets to read live
- Snippet A: metrics dashboard export (candidates -> offer -> first-week tasks) — see linked Confluence.
- Snippet B: manager feedback notes (anonymized quotes).

Open questions to ask manager
- Which of these gaps feels highest priority from your perspective?
- If we get 0.5 FTE, where would you prefer it to be allocated?
- What leadership behaviors should I demonstrate to make the promotion narrative more compelling?

Micro-phrases to use in the meeting (short, assertive)
- "I have a data-backed 6-week experiment proposal and a specific resource ask."
- "This will reduce manager time-to-onboard friction and is measurable by candidate->first-task delta."
- "My goal is to own delivery of a repeatable onboarding path that reduces variance across teams."

Notes to self after the meeting (placeholders)
- Capture manager commitments verbatim.
- Add agreed metrics to the sprint board and invite cross-functional reviewers.
- Follow up with a one-page summary and 3 next steps within 48 hours.

Unresolved/rough TODOs
- Pull last 6 months of new-hire first-week task completion rates (analytics request).
- Draft contractor job brief (1 page).
- Prepare one slide with before/after projected numbers for Q2 review.

Mental model / coaching thread (private)
- Growth = repeated stretch + fast feedback. Structure experiments so I get weekly signals, not a single outcome at week 6.
- Promotion narrative: weave together scope, influence, and repeatability (not just outputs).

Quick links I will open during the meeting
- Confluence: onboarding-playbook-draft (open)
- JIRA: HR-4821 (audit checklist)
- Slack: #people-ops / thread PLk9z7q (manager quotes)
- PR: people-ops/pull/73 (templated checklist)

Timestamped reflection (end of doc)
- 2026-03-10 09:12 — feel prepared, keep tone collaborative, lean into data-first framing.

(Short, rough — intentionally conversational. Save a final copy to Confluence if manager asks for a written plan.)
